refresh.note: Default cadences from spec section 10. seconds are poll intervals; mode websocket/stream means push delivery with the listed REST fallback.

quotes.label: Real-time quotes (BTC/ETH, US equities, FX, futures)

ui_quotes.label: UI live price tiles (maximum update rate)

ui_snapshot.label: Live dashboard check (changed prices are pushed to open pages at most this often)

ui_snapshot_full.label: Full dashboard push to open pages (at most this often, only when something besides prices changed)

hot_topics.label: Hot web-search topics (research planner; each event at most twice)

sec_filings.label: SEC filings (60 s during US market hours)

congress.label: Congress / regulation (5 min while active, 30 min otherwise)

central_banks.label: Central-bank pages (every 30 s from 15 min before to 15 min after a decision)

release_watch.label: Authoritative source during event watch mode (polled at the scheduled release second; the release schedule is checked every 5 s)

positioning.label: Futures positioning (Binance/INTX funding & OI; CFTC COT weekly, cached)

official_data.label: Official statistics (ECB, Eurostat, BLS, Treasury TGA, EIA, FRED) and central-bank state

discovery.label: Discovery sources (GDELT 15-minute batches, OFAC actions and SLS deltas, SEC full-text search)

equity_quotes.note: fixed_rate: a round starts every `seconds` (the loop sleeps seconds minus the time the round took, never less than 0), so each symbol is refreshed every 15 s instead of 15 s plus the 5-8 s the 13 sequential calls take. 13 calls x 4 rounds = 52 calls a minute, inside Finnhub's 60/min guard (symbols the guard defers are served first in the next round). The freshness limit of this feed (market_data.freshness.providers.finnhub) is sized from this interval.
equity_quotes.label: Keyed equity quotes (Finnhub primary, 13 calls per round, 60/min limit) plus the SPY/QQQ/IWM ETF proxies

alpaca_quotes.note: fixed_rate: one snapshot call every `seconds`, whatever the call took (see equity_quotes).
alpaca_quotes.label: Alpaca IEX snapshots (one call): ETF proxies (SPY, QQQ, IWM, GLD, UUP, USO, BNO) and the equities Finnhub could not serve

alpaca_bars.label: Alpaca daily bars (IEX, split-adjusted) for equities and ETF proxies: history for technical levels

alpaca_news.label: Benzinga headlines via the Alpaca News API

eia_spot.label: EIA daily spot closes for WTI and Brent (page updated weekly; conditional GET)

treasury_yields.label: US Treasury daily par yield curve closes (own loop, one attempt per hour: the file changes once per business day)

proxy_stream.label: Minimum interval between stored PAXG gold-proxy prints from the Binance stream

proxy_rest_fallback.label: PAXG gold-proxy REST fallback (Binance, then Coinbase) while the stream is silent

watch.note_time_known: Rows with time_known false (date only) or an inactive status never open a watch window or a countdown.

calendar_sources.note: Minimum seconds between fetches of a calendar source inside the calendar loop (which runs on the calendar cadence and at every release watch). Unlisted sources are fetched on every run; a failed fetch is retried on the next run.

interpretation.note: Market interpretation (backend/interpretation.py refresh): every active_seconds while any traditional market is open, otherwise idle_seconds, and immediately on the triggers below (debounced by min_interval_seconds: at most one run per 10 minutes). A run sends an AI request only when the stored AI text no longer holds or is older than unchanged_max_age_seconds, the market state was not already rejected (retry_failed_after_seconds), the provider did not just fail (retry_unavailable_after_seconds) and, for a minor change, min_ai_interval_seconds passed since the last request; otherwise the deterministic summary of the current snapshot is served. Each AI run is one request (two with a schema correction) out of the role's daily budget (ai_runtime budget.role_daily.market_interpreter). Was 300 / 900 / 60 s: 224 interpreter calls in two days, nearly all failing on timeouts or 429 and running again 5 minutes later.
interpretation.unchanged_max_age_seconds_note: An AI interpretation is kept (no new request) for up to this long while it still holds: its core (regime posture, regimes and basis, the dominant and next event with their stage, expectations and official documents, post-event divergence) is unchanged, the driver directions and the open unscheduled events are the same and every asset it names is still in the same list. The basis_hash covers those facts plus the lists' membership, trade statuses and sessions; live percentages, countdowns, windows, relevance levels and continuous scores are left out, so it does not change with every tick (measured before: 40 different hashes in 51 runs).
interpretation.min_ai_interval_seconds_note: Least time between two AI requests of the interpreter while the core is unchanged (a minor change: list membership, a driver direction, a trade status, a session, an unverified report). A change of the core (regime, dominant or next event, its stage or expectations, new official documents, a post-event divergence) is sent at once. With active_seconds 1800 this bounds a normal day at about 24 requests.
interpretation.retry_failed_after_seconds_note: A market state (basis_hash) whose AI answer was rejected is not sent again before this long has passed or the state changes; the stored interpretations rows remember it, so a restart keeps it. Measured before: 23 of 44 runs repeated an input that had already failed.
interpretation.retry_unavailable_after_seconds_note: After a request the provider did not answer (timeout, HTTP 429 or 5xx) no interpreter request is sent for this long, whatever the market state: a timed-out generation is still paid for.
interpretation.memory_rows_note: How many of the newest stored interpretations rows are read to remember rejected states and the time of the last request.
interpretation.max_brief_chars_note: Upper bound of the model input in characters (interpretation.brief): the regime summary and drivers, the dominant and next event, the lists as symbols, trade statuses and what can break. Optional parts are dropped in a fixed order until it fits. The input was about 22,000 characters before.
interpretation.max_brief_events_note: Events described to the model: the dominant one, the next one and one released event that has official documents to classify.

divergence_research.note: A post-event MARKET DIVERGENCE (event_risk trigger_state divergences / post_event research_recommended) starts one research-planner request per event through the corroborate path (planner-availability guard and search budget apply). A request that could not start is retried after retry_seconds while the event still diverges; a started one is never repeated. priority is the search-budget priority (0 = critical, as for unexplained price anomalies).

hot_topics.note: Runtime.research_hot_topics re-researches UNCONFIRMED / PARTIALLY_CONFIRMED events whose importance (source tier weight x extractor importance / 100, the tier weight alone before extraction) is at least brief.min_event_importance / 100. Events at or above urgent_min_importance get search-budget priority 0, the others priority 1. Before importance used the extractor, this cut was 0.9 on the tier weight alone (tiers 1 and 2 always urgent); 0.8 keeps an official statement the extractor rates >= 80 urgent, as alerts.event.high_importance does.
hot_topics.limits_note: Each research is one research-planner AI request (docs/AI_AGENTS.md). An event (hot topic or unconfirmed X post) is researched at most max_attempts_per_event times, and not again within recheck_hours unless new evidence reached it since the last attempt; an unexplained price anomaly (symbol and window) at most once per anomaly_recheck_hours. The attempts are stored (research_jobs 'attempts:<key>'), so a restart does not research everything again. The search-budget topic cooldown of priorities 0 and 1 is at least recheck_hours. Before: the hot-topic loop ran every 60 s and re-planned every unresolved important event each minute (1466 planner calls in two days).

triggers.note_analysis_triggers: Triggers that re-run decisions now. Event-window, regime and score triggers only refresh the interpretation: decisions carry the event overlay at read time, and a score trigger re-running decisions would feed itself.

storage.note_daily_bars: Daily bars (interval 86400) come from Alpaca, keyed by the New York session date; they are never aggregated from ticks (not in bar_intervals_seconds) and kept 800 days (>= 400 needed).
